_comment: Template, Claude Code on macOS: the fragment to MERGE into ~/.claude/settings.json; the other keys of the user's file stay as they are. One way to set it, not a requirement (guide.md); the grounds of each line, what was tried and what was only read, are in environments/claude-code-macos.md. It is one user's result of starting from Claude Code's standard configuration and adding a line only where a problem arose in use, or where the standard is known to leave a silent, irreversible harm; keep, drop or add a line by the same test. In this file a permission rule's path is ~/… or //abs — a bare /… would be relative to ~/.claude/. The read block (blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories, v2.1.257+), the write block (blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories, v2.1.314+) and the sandbox are for a user who wants nothing outside the opened folder read or written unless they ask, held by a setting and not by a model's judgement: without them, in Auto, the file tools read outside with no prompt and an outside write is the classifier's call. The write block also refuses Claude Code settings files to the agent everywhere: once it is on, the user pastes each change to this file themselves and the agent reads it back. The sandbox runs each Bash command under macOS Seatbelt — writes in the session's folders and temp alone, with the read block reads there alone, no host unless named per command and approved; the four excluded commands run outside it because git's credential comes through gh, whose folder sandboxed commands cannot read; failIfUnavailable stops the session if the sandbox cannot start, instead of running commands unsandboxed without a word. No deny line on a command name such as sudo, an installer, curl or ssh: a deny by name stops one spelling of a thing, and the sandbox bounds what any command writes and reaches. The three kept by name each print a secret: gh auth and git credential are denied whole (gh auth token, gh auth status --show-token, git credential fill; a rule matches a command's start, and signing in and out are the user's acts), security reads the keychain. Edit(**/.git/hooks/**) and Edit(**/.git/config) keep the file tools off Git's hooks and config at any depth — in the opened folder's repository and in one nested in it; the sandbox already refuses a command there, and what is planted runs at the next git push or pull, outside the sandbox. sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite carries the protection of a .claude folder's settings files and hooks from the opened folder down to a repository nested in it, for commands (a sandbox path here is anchored at ~/.claude unless it begins ~/ or /, hence ~/**). The two ask lines put before the user as a permission prompt, in every mode, every write under ~/.claude and every start of a session by a session. The mcp__ccd_* lines name tools of the Claude desktop app by which a session widens its own scope. No hooks.
